title: DOES GOD CHOOSE PEOPLE BEFORE THEY CHOOSE HIM?
paragraphs: DOES GOD CHOOSE PEOPLE BEFORE THEY CHOOSE HIM?
The question has divided dinner tables, Bible studies, seminaries, churches, and entire denominations for centuries.
Some hear that God chooses people and immediately feel comfort.
Others hear the same truth and feel resistance.
"If God chooses people, do our choices matter?"
"If God already knows everything, are we just actors reading a script?"
"Why does one person believe while another rejects Christ?"
Behind every theological debate stands something deeply personal.
A mother praying for a prodigal son.
A man wondering if God could ever want someone like him.
A woman carrying years of shame, hoping heaven has not already closed its doors.
Does God choose people before they choose Him?
The answer Scripture gives is both more mysterious and more beautiful than many realize.
And if we understand it correctly, it does not lead us into fatalism.
Because the story of salvation has never been primarily about man's search for God.
It has always been about God's relentless pursuit of man.
The scandal of grace begins there.
Long before we ever reached toward Him, He was already reaching toward us.
From the opening pages of Scripture, God is the One who initiates.
The Lord walked through the garden asking, "Where are you?" (Genesis 3:9).
The entire biblical narrative unfolds in the same pattern.
Abraham was not searching for Yahweh among the nations.
Moses was not climbing mountains looking for God.
God appeared in the burning bush.
David was not the most likely king.
The disciples were not submitting applications.
The pattern is impossible to ignore.
The New Testament speaks directly into this reality.
One of the most discussed passages appears in Ephesians 1:4:
"Even as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world."
The Greek word translated "chose" is ἐξελέξατο (exelexato).
It means to select, choose, or pick out for oneself.
The same chapter continues by saying believers were predestined according to God's purpose.
For some readers, this feels overwhelming.
Yet Paul writes these truths not to start arguments.
He writes them to inspire praise.
The chapter repeatedly erupts into worship.
Because salvation begins with God's grace, not human achievement.
If salvation ultimately depended on human goodness, no one would be saved.
"There is none righteous, no, not one."
After all, many people appear religious.
But left entirely to ourselves, we do not naturally seek the holy God who confronts our sin.
That is why Jesus said in John 6:44:
"No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him."
The Greek word for "draws" is ἑλκύσῃ (helkysē).
It carries the idea of drawing, pulling, attracting.
The Father draws sinners toward Christ.
Yet here is where many misunderstand biblical election.
God's choosing does not eliminate human responsibility.
The same Bible that teaches God's sovereignty also commands repentance and faith.
Scripture never presents people as helpless robots.
Instead, it presents salvation as a miracle where God's sovereign grace and human response operate together without contradiction.
We may not fully comprehend the mechanics.
Paul commands believers to work out their salvation with fear and trembling.
"For it is God who works in you, both to will and to work for his good pleasure."
Both truths stand side by side.
The Bible never apologizes for the mystery.
Perhaps the most beautiful picture appears in Jesus' own words.
In John 15:16, Christ tells His disciples:
"You did not choose me, but I chose you."
Imagine hearing those words from Jesus Himself.
These men likely remembered the day He walked by the sea.
The day He called their names.
What they initially thought was their decision to follow Him was actually evidence that He had already chosen them.
Grace was moving before they recognized it.
And perhaps grace was moving in your life long before you noticed it too.
Maybe you thought you discovered Christ.
Perhaps the deeper reality is that Christ was pursuing you.
Through circumstances you still cannot explain.
Looking backward, many believers eventually realize God was writing the story long before they understood the plot.
The Hebrew Scriptures reveal this same reality.
The Hebrew word often associated with God's covenantal choosing is בָּחַר (bachar).
God chose Israel not because they were greater than other nations.
Deuteronomy 7:7 explicitly says they were among the smallest.
God's choice was rooted in His love.
The same principle echoes throughout redemption history.
This is where the Gospel becomes breathtaking.
Because if God's choice depended on human perfection, no one would qualify.
But because grace triumphs over scandal.
The cross proves this more powerfully than any theological argument.
Think about the thief hanging beside Jesus.
"Today you will be with me in Paradise."
At that moment, heaven's doors opened to a scandalous sinner.
That truth should humble every believer.
None of us stand before God because we were smarter.
Every testimony ultimately begins with divine grace.
Every redeemed life is evidence that God still specializes in rewriting impossible stories.
Because God not only ordains the end.
The God who saves people also sends people.
The same Jesus who taught divine election also commanded His followers:
"Go therefore and make disciples of all nations."
The apostles never saw evangelism and election as enemies.
Because we do not know whom God will save.
And we trust God to do what only God can do.
The Gospel invitation remains gloriously open.
The very hunger drawing you toward Him may be evidence that His grace has already been pursuing you.
No one who comes to Christ will be cast out.
The deeper one studies election, the less it becomes about winning theological arguments and the more it becomes about worship.
Because salvation is not ultimately the story of humanity climbing toward God.
It is the story of God descending toward humanity.
God transforming sinners into sons and daughters.
That is why the Gospel remains the greatest scandal ever told.
The Holy One loves the unholy.
The Perfect One dies for the guilty.
Maybe that is your story too.
Maybe you've spent years believing you were too far gone.
But Scripture tells a different story.
The God who welcomed the thief on the cross.
And perhaps the strongest evidence that God chooses people before they choose Him is this:
Long before you ever wondered about Him...
He was already thinking about you.
Have you ever looked back and realized God was pursuing you long before you recognized Him?
The God you thought you were searching for may have been searching for you all along.
